cross_review: This is a cross-review, not final synthesis: do not add a PR metadata header or an introductory/progress sentence. Use the stage language resolved by the orchestrator.
Format the result for fast scanning.

Use one row per atomic claim. If a source finding contains both true and false claims, split it into separate rows so every classification remains exactly CONFIRMED, REJECTED, or UNCERTAIN. For a confirmed finding, Severity must be exactly P0, P1, P2, or P3; use — only when severity does not apply. Keep code evidence concise but concrete in the Verification column. Mark duplicates explicitly in that column and reference the canonical row.

If validation discovers genuinely new findings, add a separate section named ## New findings with the same table shape. Follow the additional report structure supplied by the orchestrator; do not add sections that the resolved reporting configuration disables.
final: The orchestrator writes the PR title and two-column metadata table. Do not output or repeat them.
Do not write an introduction such as ‘I have verified…’ or ‘Let me synthesize…’. The orchestrator supplies the required first heading and localized table format.

Write the main final review in the resolved global/stage language selected by the orchestrator. Follow its resolved reporting structure and localized headings/table schemas. Every CONFIRMED row must use exactly P0, P1, P2, or P3; use — only when severity does not apply. Include detailed sections only for actionable, source-verified CONFIRMED findings.
At the very end, add two separate sections containing polished English comments ready to paste directly into the pull request:

Include must-fix P0/P1 comments. Each comment must identify the location, explain the concrete failure or risk, and request a specific change. Do not mention internal reviewer names or the orchestration process.
Include non-blocking P2/P3 comments using the same author-facing style. If either section has no comments, write None.
